title_en.text: Panas Falls (New Corella, Davao del Norte)

tagline.text: Turquoise tiered falls in New Corella's protected forest

location.label: Location
location.text: Brgy. Carcor, New Corella, Davao del Norte (Panas Waterfalls Eco-Cultural Park)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (day trip from Davao City, including entrance fee, transport and food)

children.text: Panas Falls is a municipality-run eco-cultural park inside a protected forest in Barangay Carcor, New Corella. A main fall about 9m high, a turquoise plunge pool and shallow natural pools make it a great family swimming spot.

Panas Falls is a waterfall and park in Barangay Carcor, New Corella, Davao del Norte, officially called Panas Waterfalls Eco-Cultural Park. It lies inside a forest designated as a protected area and is run directly by the New Corella local government unit (LGU) as a resort-style park, so fees are lower and operations simpler than at privately run sites.
Rather than a single big fall, it is a cluster of tiered falls and spring-fed pools. Travel media describe the largest tier as a rock face about
9m

(roughly 30 feet) high, with a cold, clear turquoise basin at its foot. Higher up are low cascades, natural pools that are safe for swimming, and man-made pools, so it is not stressful to bring children.
The park is about
2 hours
by road from Davao City, about
25–30 minutes
from Tagum City and about
10–20 minutes

from New Corella town proper. The road is described as paved, but past visitors reported it turning muddy in the rain, so check conditions in the wet season. It makes an easy northern day trip to free up between longer outings such as Samal Island or Mount Apo.

This is not a crowded, famous attraction. Before COVID-19 it was said to be full of visitors on weekends, and since then many days have been quiet. It suits anyone who wants to relax to the sound of water in a quiet forest; if you expect polished facilities or a restaurant row, you may be disappointed. Families should bring a packed lunch and a mat and treat it as a half-day picnic. New Corella is one of the quieter municipalities in Davao del Norte, so you can also take in modest local life such as the town market, small eateries and farm stays, which is part of its charm.
The largest tier of the park, where water tumbles down a rock face and sends turquoise spray into the pool below. The loud, cooling roar makes this the spot where the trip feels most worthwhile.
The pool below the fall is cold and clear, ideal for cooling off in the midday heat. Depth varies by area, so follow the signs and staff advice and enter from the edge.
Higher up, low cascades and shallow natural pools follow one another. Travel media describe this area as safe for swimming, so it is the most comfortable place for families with children.
Local media describe the site as a complex of spring-fed natural pools, a freshwater lagoon and waterfalls. Children who are uneasy in the stream can play in the shallow man-made pools.
You can enjoy light walks through the protected forest or trek upstream along the creek. Wear shoes that are fine to get wet and ask staff about safe sections first.
There are cottages near the water, and visitors can reportedly bring uncooked meat to grill in the grill area. If you plan to stay all day, renting a cottage is the most practical choice.

Even without swimming, simply resting among green trees and the sound of water is restorative. Local visitors say it is a good place for families and friends to gather and unwind, almost like meditating.

items.title: Day trip from Davao
items.subtitle: Leave in the morning, return in the afternoon

children.text: Take a bus to Tagum from a bus terminal in Davao City. Depending on traffic, it takes about
1–1.5 hours
In Tagum City, transfer to a jeepney bound for New Corella and ask the driver to drop you at Panas Eco-Cultural Park.
From New Corella town, a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) reaches the park in about
10–20 minutes
. Arrange your ride back in advance.
Pay the entrance fee, rent a cottage and unpack. Start by getting wet in the shallow upper pools.
See the main fall and its pool, then swim in a safe area.
Eat a packed lunch and rest in the shade. There is reportedly no restaurant inside the park.
Pack up, take a motorcycle taxi back to town and head toward Tagum.

The park's closing time is not well documented publicly. Try to leave early in the afternoon, and check with the New Corella tourism office before your visit. Travel to and from Davao City adds up to about
4–5 hours
, so a realistic swimming time is about 3–4 hours.

items.title: A full day in New Corella
items.subtitle: Falls and farm stay

children.text: Hire a rental car or local driver in Tagum City and head to New Corella.
Reach Panas Eco-Cultural Park first, while it is quiet, and take photos and swim.
Have lunch and rest.
Look around farm stays near town, such as Willax Farm, which local media have featured, or continue to attractions in nearby Kapalong.
Return to Tagum City for dinner.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Francisco Bangoy International Airport, Davao (DVO), taking about
1 hour 50 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change often, so check when you book.
From Davao Airport, take a taxi or Grab to the city, then head to a bus terminal for buses toward Tagum in the north.
Most Philippine airlines connect Manila and Davao daily.
Take a bus bound for Tagum from a bus terminal in Davao City, then take a jeepney bound for New Corella in Tagum City.
Some guides say jeepneys leave from a stop near the Tagum City Overland Transport Integrated Terminal (TCOTIT), so confirm on site.

items.title: From New Corella to the park

children.text: Habal-habal run from New Corella town to Panas in about
10–20 minutes
, reportedly for a modest fare. Ask for the round-trip price before bargaining.
There is reportedly no public transport from the park back to town, so it is safer to book your return motorcycle ride in advance.
Search for Panas Eco-Cultural Park in Google Maps or Waze. Parking is available inside the park.
It takes about
25–30 minutes
from Tagum City and about
2 hours
from Davao City.

Local media name the hot summer (dry season) as the best time for waterfall swimming, because the cold water is especially welcome under strong sun. However, rain in Davao del Norte is fairly evenly spread through the year, so the dry and wet seasons are not clear-cut; check the forecast before you leave.

Right after heavy rain the water volume rises sharply, the water can turn muddy and the access path becomes slippery. For safety, postpone your visit the day after heavy rain or when a heavy-rain warning is in effect.

On weekends, holidays and school breaks, local family groups increase and cottages may fill up first. For a quiet visit, arrive on a weekday morning; groups should contact the park beforehand to confirm cottage and function hall availability.

There is reportedly no restaurant inside the park. Nearby shops sell drinks and light snacks, but choices are limited, so bring a packed lunch and plenty of drinking water. A grill area is available, and you can bring uncooked meat to grill.

You can use a dormitory-style room or cottage inside the park, but most travelers stay in Davao City or Tagum City and visit as a day trip. Tagum offers hotels and restaurants nearly as varied as Davao, making it a good place to stay a night before or after New Corella.

New Corella town has a market, small eateries and convenience-style shops, so it is a good place to buy water, snacks and ice before you go. Shops near the park may not keep regular hours, so it is safer to prepare what you need in town. If you plan to use the charcoal grill, also bring charcoal, seasoning, cooking tools and disposable plates.
Before you go, check opening hours and fees with the New Corella tourism office through its Facebook page (TourismNewCorella) or the posted contact numbers.
When you take a habal-habal from town to the park, tell the driver when you will return and agree on a round trip.
The water is cold and the rocks are slippery, so wear aqua shoes or non-slip sandals.
Pack spare clothes, a towel, a waterproof bag and a trash bag. Take your trash back with you.
Cottages come in big and small sizes, so choose by group size and arrive early on weekends.
Bring plenty of cash in pesos. Do not count on cashless payment.
On the day you land at Davao Airport, rest in Davao City and travel the next day to be safe.
Avoid entering the water right after rain, when the flow rises and the rocks are very slippery, and follow staff instructions.
Water depth is uneven in the pool below the fall and around the rocks. Children must always be supervised by an adult.
The park may not have enough rescue equipment or medical facilities, so bring basic medicines.
There is no public transport back to town, so it is best to leave before sunset.
Mobile signal may be weak, so save an offline map.
Much of the fee and facility information dates from 2018–2021. Check the latest announcements.
This is a protected forest, so do not pick plants or catch animals, and do not use soap or shampoo in the falls.
A good base, about
2 hours
away by road. The airport, hotels and restaurants are concentrated here.
The nearest large city to New Corella, about
25–30 minutes
away, and a transfer point for transport.
Local media feature Tagtugonan Falls, Okbot Cave and Linow tu Gabon in Kapalong. The distance from Panas was not confirmed, so ask locally.
Presented as a farm-style cottage stay about
15 minutes
by road from New Corella town. Check its operating status locally.
